name: Cream of Something Soup
notes: A good way to use up that powdered milk and make a healthy economical meal! *This white sauce is the same that’s used to make gravy for fried chicken and biscuits and gravy—just use the drippings leftover from cooking the meat.

items: Bacon or ham, if you have some
Broccoli, potatoes, beans, carrot, cauliflower, etc. (unless using corn or other canned vegetable, which is added at the end)
A small amount of water, to steam the vegetables
Chicken base, pepper and hot sauce, to taste

steps.title: Sauté the onion
steps.body: In a good-sized pot, sauté **1 onion**, chopped, and bacon or ham if you have some.

steps.title: Steam the vegetables
steps.body: When onion is tender and the bacon is crisp, add a small amount of water and steam the vegetables you have chosen until tender: broccoli, potatoes, beans, carrot, cauliflower, etc. Unless you’re using corn or other canned vegetable, which can be added at the end.

steps.title: Make the white sauce
steps.body: Whisk together a basic medium white sauce* (multiply according to quantity of vegetables and eaters—this will make soup for about 2 people): **2 cups water**, **⅓ cup powdered milk** and **¼ cup flour**.

steps.title: Thicken the soup
steps.body: Pour whisked mixture into soup pot and cook, stirring occasionally, on medium heat until thick. Don’t let this boil—it separates and will not thicken. Season with chicken base, pepper and hot sauce to taste. Garnish with a bit of cheese and serve to a hungry crew.
